sections.h2: Companies that would leave are 46.2% of spenders but hold 3.1% of the money

chart.title: Leavers are close to half of spenders but about 3% of the money
chart.sub: Share of CSR spenders and of CSR money, %.
chart.source: MCA estimate of 2025-26 obligation vs 2024-25 spend; IICA India CSR Factbook 2024-25.
rows: Their obligation, share of CSR money

sections.means: The 11,204 companies that would leave are about 46% of CSR spenders, but their obligation is about 3.1% of the money.
sections.todo: Ask the ministry to publish which states and causes the Rs 1,282 crore estimate reaches before the Bill is passed.

sections.h2: 93 firms spending Rs 50 crore or more give 42.4% of CSR money

chart.title: Most CSR money comes from a few large spenders, not many small ones
chart.sub: Share of the Rs 40,794 crore spent in 2024-25, %.
chart.source: IICA India CSR Factbook 2024-25, from the MCA National CSR Data Portal.

sections.means: Most spenders are small, but the 93 largest firms hold 42.4% of CSR money, so the small-firm exit moves few rupees.
sections.todo: Publish spend shares for the Rs 1-10 cr and Rs 10-50 cr bands separately, which the Factbook gives only together.

sections.h2: Reported CSR spending rose from Rs 10,066 crore to Rs 40,794 crore since 2014-15

chart.title: Reported CSR spend rose from Rs 10,066 crore in FY15 to Rs 40,794 crore in FY25
chart.sub: Reported CSR spend, Rs crore. FY19 to FY21 are earlier portal snapshots, not strictly comparable.

sections.means: Reported CSR spend grew 13% to 17% a year in each of the last three years, so the loss from the Bill is small by comparison.
sections.todo: Check actual 2025-26 CSR spending against the ministry's Rs 1,282 crore estimate once the Factbook reports it.
